sentences.text: It was submitted that claimant aged 60 years and earning Rs.10,000/- per month from agriculture, sustained fracture of shaft of right clavicle.
It was submitted that Tribunal considered lower monthly income of Rs.6,000/- while assessing compensation.
Even disability considered was on lower side.
Further, award of Rs.10,000/- towards loss of amenities, Rs.18,000/- towards loss of income during laid up period and Rs.2,000/- towards attendant charges required enhancement.
On above grounds, sought for allowing appeal.
On other hand, Sri Manjunath Mallayya Shetty, learned counsel for respondent no.3 and Sudhir Singh R. Vijapur, learned counsel for respondent no.5 sought to support impugned award.

4. Heard learned counsel and perused impugned judgment and award and copies of discharge summary and disability certificate made available by learned counsel for claimant.
5.

From above submission and since only claimant was in appeal for enhancement, point that arises for consideration is:
 "Whether claimant is entitled for  enhancement of compensation as sought  for?"
6.
Though claimant stated that she was earning Rs.10,000/- per month from agriculture, same is not substantiated with evidence.
In absence same, income has to be assessed notionally.
Notional income for year 2013 (date of accident) is Rs.7,000/-.
Therefore, same NC: 2023:KHC-K:6473 has to be considered.

Referring to treatment records and deposition of PW.2, Tribunal observed that claimant had sustained fracture of lateral third shaft of right clavicle, which as per Ex.P10 - disability certificate was mal-united.
On ground that disability assessed by doctor was on higher side, it considered loss of earning capacity at 5%.
On perusal of discharge summary, it is seen that nature of treatment administered was conservative.
Further, fracture of clavicle would normally not result in loss of earning capacity.
It is considered ornamental bone.

Under such circumstances,
assessment of disability by Tribunal would not call for interference.

Thus, future loss of income would be:
Rs.7,000/- x 5% x 12 x 9 = Rs.37,800/-
7. Rs.30,000/- awarded towards pain and suffering and Rs.11,689/- awarded towards medical expenses would be appropriate.
Likewise, Rs.2,000/- awarded towards attendance and other incidental expenses for in-patient treatment period of four days NC: 2023:KHC-K:6473 would also be appropriate.

But, considering disability sustained due to mal-union, award of Rs.10,000/-
towards loss of amenities would be inadequate and same is enhanced to Rs.30,000/-.

Consequently, following:
ORDER i. Appeal is allowed-in-part with costs.
ii. Claimant is held entitled for total compensation of Rs.1,32,489/- with interest at 6% p.a. from date of claim petition till deposit.
iii. Respondent no.3-insurer to deposit enhanced compensation within six weeks from date of receipt of certified copy of this order.
